Full Solution: Bandura identifies four mediational processes: Attention (noticing the model), Retention (remembering the action), Reproduction (physical ability to copy), and Motivation (will to perform). The scenario describes a change in performance frequency due to observed consequences (vicarious reinforcement), which directly activates the Motivational process—the student expects similar praise, providing the incentive to act.
questions.topic: Bandura's Social Learning Theory - Observational Learning

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the number obtained by raising 7 to the power of 45 (7^45)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The unit digit of powers of 7 follows a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Divide the exponent 45 by 4; the remainder is 1. The 1st value in the cycle is 7. Step-by-step: 7^1=7, 7^2=49, 7^3=343, 7^4=2401. The cycle (7, 9, 3, 1) repeats every 4 powers. 45 = 4 × 11 + 1, so the unit digit corresponds to 7^1, which is 7.

questions.text: A train is moving at a speed of 72 km/h. What is its speed in metres per second (m/s)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by the factor 5/18. Calculation: 72 × (5/18) = (72/18) × 5 = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s. Step-by-step: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 hour = 3600 seconds. Speed in m/s = (72 × 1000) / 3600 = 72000 / 3600 = 720 / 36 = 20 m/s.

questions.text: According to Van Hiele's levels of geometric thinking, a student identifies a rectangle solely by saying, 'It looks like a door' or 'It looks like a blackboard,' without referencing its properties like parallel sides or right angles. This student is operating at which level?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Level 0 (Visualization) is defined by recognition based on overall visual appearance/gestalt ('looks like'), not properties. Level 1 involves property identification. Step-by-step: Van Hiele Level 0: Students recognize shapes by visual likeness to real-world objects. Level 1: Students analyze properties (e.g., '4 right angles'). Level 2: Students establish relationships (e.g., 'Square is a rectangle'). The student's reasoning ('looks like a door') matches Level 0 exactly.
questions.topic: Pedagogy - Van Hiele Levels of Geometric Thinking

questions.text: As per the table showing the energy available at different trophic levels in a grassland ecosystem, if the energy at the Producer level (Grass) is 10,000 Joules, what will be the approximate energy available at the Secondary Consumer level (Frog) according to Lindeman's 10% Law?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the 10% energy transfer rule twice (Producer → Primary → Secondary). 10,000 J → 1,000 J (Primary) → 100 J (Secondary). Select 100 J. Step-by-step: Lindeman's 10% Law states only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level. Energy at Producer level = 10,000 J. Energy at Primary Consumer (Grasshopper) = 10% of 10,000 = 1,000 J. Energy at Secondary Consumer (Frog) = 10% of 1,000 = 100 J.

questions.text: As per the bar chart showing the approximate decomposition time of common waste materials in a landfill, which material takes the longest time to decompose?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the material persistence hierarchy: Organic materials (Paper, Cotton) decompose in weeks/months; Synthetic polymers (Plastic) take decades; Metals (Aluminum) take centuries. The tallest bar (Aluminum Can) represents the longest time. Step-by-step: Paper decomposes in 2–5 weeks. Cotton cloth takes 2–5 months. Plastic bags take 10–20 years (up to 500 years for complete breakdown). Aluminum cans take 80–200 years to oxidize and decompose. Thus, Aluminum Can has the longest decomposition time.

questions.text: A Class IV EVS teacher wants to assess the process skill of 'Observation and Recording' in the theme 'Plants Around Us'. Which of the following assessment strategies is MOST appropriate for this specific skill?

options.label: A
options.text: Taking students on a nature walk to observe local plants and asking them to record the leaf shape, venation, and texture in their observation notebooks.

options.label: B
options.text: Asking students to write down the definitions of 'Photosynthesis' and 'Transpiration' from the textbook.

options.label: C
options.text: Conducting a multiple-choice test on the functions of root, stem, and leaf.

options.label: D
options.text: Asking students to draw and label the diagram of a 'Typical Flower' from memory.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options testing only memory/recall (B, C, D). Option A is the only one requiring real-time sensory engagement (observation) and simultaneous documentation (recording) in an authentic environment. Step-by-step: 'Observation and Recording' involves using senses to gather first-hand data and documenting it immediately. Option B tests rote memorization of definitions. Option C tests recognition/recall of theoretical knowledge. Option D tests reproduction of a memorized diagram. Option A requires students to observe live specimens, discriminate features (shape, venation, texture), and record findings directly, aligning perfectly with the skill.
questions.topic: EVS Pedagogy - Assessment of Process Skills

questions.text: According to Noam Chomsky's theory of language acquisition, the 'Language Acquisition Device' (LAD) is a hypothetical innate mechanism that enables children to:

options.label: A
options.text: Imitate adult speech perfectly through repeated practice.

options.label: B
options.text: Deduce the underlying grammatical rules of any language they are exposed to.

options.label: C
options.text: Associate specific words with objects through classical conditioning.

options.label: D
options.text: Develop language solely based on the frequency of linguistic input received.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options reflecting Behaviorist theory (imitation, conditioning, input frequency). LAD represents the Nativist view of innate grammatical competence. Worked Solution: Chomsky proposed LAD as an innate biological endowment containing Universal Grammar, allowing children to unconsciously hypothesize and internalize the syntactic rules of their specific language environment, rather than merely mimicking or being conditioned.

questions.text: A primary school teacher uses 'exit tickets' where students write one thing they learned and one question they still have at the end of a lesson. The teacher uses this data to plan the next day's remedial activity. This practice is a classic example of:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify keywords 'uses data to plan next day's remedial activity' indicating immediate instructional adjustment; eliminate 'end-of-term' (Summative), 'external comparison' (Standardized), and 'self-regulation' (Metacognitive) options. Worked Solution: Formative Assessment (Assessment for Learning) is conducted during the instructional process to provide continuous feedback to both teacher and learner, enabling timely modification of teaching strategies to address learning gaps, unlike summative assessment which evaluates learning at the end.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used in the following sentence: "Her voice was a soothing melody that calmed the restless crowd."
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Simile (requires 'like' or 'as'), Personification (attributes human traits to non-human), and Hyperbole (intentional exaggeration); the direct equation 'voice was a melody' signals Metaphor. Worked Solution: A Metaphor makes an implicit comparison between two unlike things by stating one *is* the other. Here, 'voice' is directly equated to 'a soothing melody' without comparative words, transferring the qualities of melody (soothing, musical) to the voice.

questions.text: Choose the correct indirect speech transformation of the following direct speech: He said, "I am writing a letter."

options.label: A
options.text: He said that he is writing a letter.

options.label: B
options.text: He said that he was writing a letter.

options.label: C
options.text: He said that I was writing a letter.

options.label: D
options.text: He said that he will write a letter.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options where the tense does not shift back (Present Continuous → Past Continuous) or the pronoun 'I' remains unchanged. Option A fails tense shift; Option C fails pronoun change; Option D changes meaning/tense incorrectly. Worked Solution: Reporting verb 'said' (past) triggers backshift. 'I' becomes 'he'. 'am writing' (Present Continuous) becomes 'was writing' (Past Continuous). Result: He said that he was writing a letter.

questions.text: Which of the following is a core principle of Communicative Language Teaching (CLT)?

options.label: A
options.text: Primary focus on explicit grammar rules and structural accuracy through drills.

options.label: B
options.text: Memorization of scripted dialogues to achieve native-like pronunciation.

options.label: C
options.text: Interaction as both the means and the ultimate goal of language learning.

options.label: D
options.text: Immediate correction of all learner errors to prevent fossilization.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options reflecting Grammar-Translation (A), Audio-Lingual Method (B, D). CLT keywords: 'Communication', 'Interaction', 'Fluency', 'Meaning over Form'. Worked Solution: CLT emphasizes communicative competence. It posits that language is acquired through meaningful interaction (means) to enable real-life communication (goal). It tolerates errors as natural to interlanguage development and uses authentic materials rather than scripted drills.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech in the following sentence: "The wind whispered secrets through the trees."
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check for human qualities (whispered) given to non-human subject (wind) without comparison words 'like/as'. Eliminate Simile (no like/as), Metaphor (no direct 'is' comparison), Hyperbole (no exaggeration). Worked Solution: 'Wind' is an inanimate force; 'whispered' is a deliberate human vocal action requiring intent. Attributing this human action to the wind constitutes Personification. A Simile would use 'like/as' (e.g., 'wind sounded like a whisper'). A Metaphor would state 'The wind was a whisperer'. Hyperbole would exaggerate (e.g., 'The wind screamed loud enough to shatter glass').

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 15% and 10% on the marked price of an article. What is the equivalent single discount percentage?
questions.solution: Assume marked price = 100. After 15% discount → 85. After 10% discount → 85 × 0.90 = 76.5. Total discount = 100 − 76.5 = 23.5. Equivalent single discount = 23.5%.

questions.text: A 120‑litre vessel contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 5. First, 30 litres of the mixture is drawn out and replaced with water. Next, 20 litres of the new mixture is drawn out and replaced with pure milk. What is the final ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.solution:
1. Initial milk = 7/12×120 = 70 L, water = 50 L.
2. Remove 30 L (7:5) → milk left = 70−30×7/12 = 52.5 L, water left = 50−30×5/12 = 37.5 L.
3. Add 30 L water → water = 37.5+30 = 67.5 L (total 120 L).
4. New ratio milk:water = 52.5:67.5 = 7:9.
5. Remove 20 L → milk removed = 20×7/16 = 8.75 L, water removed = 20×9/16 = 11.25 L.
6. Remaining milk = 52.5−8.75 = 43.75 L, water = 67.5−11.25 = 56.25 L.
7. Add 20 L milk → milk = 43.75+20 = 63.75 L, water = 56.25 L.
8. Final ratio = 63.75:56.25 = 17:15.
questions.style: Variable Volume Replacement with Additive Step

questions.text: A person invests Rs. 50,000 at 10% p.a. compound interest compounded annually. After 2 years, he withdraws Rs. 10,000. The remaining amount is then invested at 12% p.a. compound interest compounded annually for another 2 years. What is the total amount at the end of 4 years?
questions.solution:
1. Amount after 2 years at 10% CI = 50000 × (1.10)² = 60,500.
2. After withdrawal of 10,000, principal = 50,500.
3. Amount after next 2 years at 12% CI = 50,500 × (1.12)² = 50,500 × 1.2544 = 63,347.20.
4. Final amount = Rs. 63,347.20.
questions.style: Variable Rate Compound Interest with Mid-term Withdrawal

questions.text: The new policy will ______ the small businesses positively, allowing them to expand their operations.
questions.solution:
1. The blank follows the modal verb "will", so a base-form verb is required.
2. "affect" is a verb meaning to influence; "effect" is primarily a noun meaning result.
3. "infect" (to contaminate) and "defect" (a flaw) are semantically unrelated.
4. Only "affect" fits both grammatically and contextually.

questions.text: The ministry is ______ to implement the new policy by next quarter.
questions.solution:
1. The subject "ministry" and the context "policy" require a formal official tone.
2. Only "committed" forms the standard formal collocation "committed to implement" in administrative language.
3. "Keen to", "eager to", and "willing to" are informal or personal‑intent expressions.
4. Therefore the correct word is "committed".

questions.text:
Read the passage and choose the word which best replaces the underlined word.

"The new railway subsidy scheme, though hailed as a panacea by many officials, has inadvertently *exacerbated* the financial strain on small freight operators, many of whom are now forced to curtail services."

The word *exacerbated* most nearly means:
questions.solution: 1. Identify meaning of 'exacerbated' in context: it worsens a problem. 2. Options A (alleviated) and C (mitigated) mean to lessen, opposite meaning. 3. Option D (simplified) unrelated. 4. Only option B (intensified) matches 'worsen'.

questions.text: The ______ of the new railway safety protocol was ______ by the committee after the trial run.
questions.solution:
1. First blank follows 'The' and precedes 'of', so it must be a noun. Only 'evaluation' is a noun; 'evaluative' is an adjective.
2. Second blank follows 'was' and precedes 'by', requiring a past participle verb for passive voice. Only 'evaluated' fits; 'evaluative' is an adjective.
3. The correct pair 'evaluation, evaluated' shares the root 'evalu-', satisfying morphological derivation consistency.
4. All other options violate either grammatical requirement or root consistency.

questions.text: A courier bike travels from Point X to Point Y at 40 km/h and returns along the same route at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.solution:
Let one-way distance = d km.
Time onward = d/40 h, return = d/60 h.
Total distance = 2d, total time = d/40 + d/60 = 5d/120 = d/24 h.
Average speed = 2d / (d/24) = 48 km/h.

questions.text: A retail outlet marks the price of a television at Rs M. It first offers a flat 20% discount on the marked price and then provides an additional cash rebate of Rs 150 on the discounted amount. If a customer pays Rs 1,350 for the TV, what was the original marked price Rs M?
questions.solution:
Let M be the marked price.
Discounted price = M − 20% of M = 0.8M.
After rebate: 0.8M − 150 = 1,350.
0.8M = 1,500.
M = 1,500 ÷ 0.8 = 1,875.
Thus the marked price is Rs 1,875.

questions.text: A tea seller mixes 5 kg of Grade‑A tea priced at Rs 120 per kg with 3 kg of Grade‑B tea priced at Rs 200 per kg. He then offers a flat 10 % discount on the total cost of the mixed tea. What is the final selling price per kilogram after the discount?
questions.solution:
1. Cost of Grade‑A = 5 kg × 120 = Rs 600.
2. Cost of Grade‑B = 3 kg × 200 = Rs 600.
3. Total cost before discount = 600 + 600 = Rs 1,200.
4. Total weight = 5 kg + 3 kg = 8 kg.
5. Discount = 10 % of 1,200 = Rs 120.
6. Payable amount = 1,200 - 120 = Rs 1,080.
7. Final price per kg = 1,080 ÷ 8 = Rs 135.
8. Hence, Rs 135 per kg is the correct answer.

questions.text: Two trains start simultaneously from stations P and Q towards each other. After crossing each other, train A takes 4 hours to reach Q and train B takes 9 hours to reach P. If the distance between P and Q is 150 km, find the speed of train A.
questions.solution: Let speeds be Va and Vb. After meeting, distance covered by A before meeting = Vb × 9 (since B covers it in 9 h). Distance covered by B before meeting = Va × 4. So Va/Vb = (Vb×9)/(Va×4) ⇒ (Va/Vb)² = 9/4 ⇒ Va/Vb = 3/2. Let Va = 3x, Vb = 2x. Total distance = distance before meeting = Vb×9 + Va×4 = 2x×9 + 3x×4 = 30x. Given 30x = 150 ⇒ x = 5. Hence Va = 3×5 = 15 km/h.

questions.text: A person deposits Rs 10,000 in a bank offering simple interest at 8% per annum for the first 2 years. After 2 years the rate changes to 10% per annum for the next 3 years. At the end of the 2nd year he deposits an additional Rs 5,000. What is the total amount at the end of 5 years?
questions.solution:
Interest on Rs 10,000 for first 2 yr @8% = 10000×0.08×2 = 1600.
Interest on Rs 10,000 for next 3 yr @10% = 10000×0.10×3 = 3000.
Interest on additional Rs 5,000 for 3 yr @10% = 5000×0.10×3 = 1500.
Total interest = 1600+3000+1500 = 6100.
Total principal = 10000+5000 = 15000.
Amount = 15000+6100 = 21100.
questions.style: Staggered Deposit Simple Interest with Rate Change

questions.text: A contractor secures a job worth Rs 48,000. Three workers A, B and C can complete the whole job alone in 10, 15 and 30 days respectively. They start together and work for 3 days, after which A leaves. B and C finish the remaining work in 4 more days. The daily wage for each worker present is Rs 800. What is the contractor’s profit after paying the wages?
questions.solution:
1. Rates: A=1/10, B=1/15, C=1/30 per day.
2. Combined rate =1/10+1/15+1/30 = (3+2+1)/30 =6/30 =1/5 of work per day.
3. Work done in 3 days =3×1/5 =3/5.
4. Remaining work =1‑3/5 =2/5.
5. B+C rate =1/15+1/30 = (2+1)/30 =3/30 =1/10 per day.
6. Days needed for 2/5 work = (2/5) ÷ (1/10) = (2/5)×10 =4 days (matches statement).
7. Wage cost: first 3 days → 3 workers × Rs800 ×3 = Rs7,200.
   Next 4 days → 2 workers × Rs800 ×4 = Rs6,400.
   Total wage =7,200+6,400 = Rs13,600.
8. Profit = Contract amount – Wage = 48,000 – 13,600 = Rs34,400.

questions.text: A retailer purchases 120 units of a gadget at Rs 45 each. He sells 30 units at a 20% profit and 50 units at a 10% loss. The remaining units are sold at a single uniform price so that his overall profit on the whole purchase is exactly 8%. What is the selling price per unit of the remaining units?
questions.solution:
1. Total cost =120×45=Rs 5400.
2. Desired overall profit =8% ⇒ required total revenue =5400×1.08=Rs 5832.
3. Revenue from first 30 units (20% profit): cost 30×45=1350; revenue=1350×1.20=Rs 1620.
4. Revenue from next 50 units (10% loss): cost 50×45=2250; revenue=2250×0.90=Rs 2025.
5. Let price of each of the remaining 40 units be p. Then revenue from them =40p.
6. Total revenue =1620+2025+40p =5832.
7. 40p =5832−3645 =2187 ⇒ p =2187/40 = Rs 54.675.
8. Hence the uniform selling price of the remaining units is Rs 54.675 per unit.

questions.text: The new policy aims to reduce waste, ______ it also encourages recycling among citizens.
questions.solution:
1. The clause before the blank states an aim (reduce waste).
2. The clause after the blank adds another positive action (encourages recycling).
3. The relationship is addition, not contrast or result.
4. 'Moreover' is an additive connector; the others express contrast or consequence.

questions.text: The government's new initiative seeks to ______ the gap between digital literacy and employment opportunities in rural areas.
questions.solution: The phrase "bridge the gap" is a fixed idiom meaning to reduce or eliminate a disparity. While "fill", "close", and "reduce" can collocate with "gap", the standard expression in policy contexts is "bridge the gap". Hence the correct choice is "bridge".

questions.text: While the government's new scheme seeks to alleviate the financial strain on marginal farmers, it inadvertently ______ the administrative burden on state agencies.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the discourse marker "While" at the start – it signals a contrast between the two clauses.
2. The first clause uses "alleviate" (meaning to reduce or ease).
3. Because of the contrast, the second clause must express the opposite effect – an increase in burden.
4. Among the options, only "escalate" means to increase or intensify.
5. "Mitigate", "lessen", and "curtail" are synonyms of "alleviate" and would continue the same direction, violating the contrast.
6. Therefore the correct fill is "escalate".

questions.text:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows:

"The new railway safety protocol, introduced after a series of minor accidents, mandates that train operators must *eschew* any form of complacency during peak hours. Instead of relying on routine checks alone, they are required to *scrutinize* each signal with heightened vigilance, ensuring that no oversight compromises passenger safety. This proactive stance has been praised for its *efficacy* in reducing delays and accidents."

Which word from the passage is closest in meaning to the word "eschew" as used in the first sentence?

A) Embrace
B) Avoid
C) Encourage
D) Tolerate
questions.solution: The word "eschew" means to deliberately avoid or keep away from. Among the options, only "Avoid" matches this meaning. Hence option B is correct.

questions.text: A 7-year-old child finds a lost wallet in the school corridor and immediately hands it over to the teacher, stating, "If I keep it, the police will catch me and I will be punished." According to Lawrence Kohlberg's theory of moral development, this reasoning is characteristic of which specific stage?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Spot the keyword "punished" or "fear of authority". In Kohlberg's Pre-conventional level, Stage 1 is defined solely by avoiding punishment. Stage 2 involves self-interest ('what's in it for me?'), while Stages 3 and 4 belong to the Conventional level (peer approval/law & order). Eliminate options B, C, D based on level mismatch. Full Solution: Lawrence Kohlberg's Stage 1 (Obedience and Punishment Orientation) is the earliest stage of moral reasoning, typically found in young children. The child judges the morality of an action by its direct consequences—specifically, the fear of punishment from authority figures (police/teacher). The statement "I will be punished" is the definitive marker for Stage 1. Stage 2 focuses on instrumental exchange ('you scratch my back...'), Stage 3 on being a 'good person' to gain approval, and Stage 4 on upholding laws to maintain societal order.

questions.text: A student demonstrates a profound ability to recognize and classify numerous species of birds, insects, and plants during a nature walk. The student easily identifies ecological patterns and shows deep concern for environmental conservation. According to Howard Gardner's Theory of Multiple Intelligences, this student exhibits a dominant strength in which intelligence?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Map keywords "classify species", "ecological patterns", "nature walk", "environment" directly to Naturalistic Intelligence. Logical-Mathematical deals with abstract numbers/patterns; Spatial deals with visual imagery/navigation; Bodily-Kinesthetic deals with physical movement/coordination. Eliminate A, C, D by domain mismatch. Full Solution: Howard Gardner added Naturalistic Intelligence as the eighth intelligence (1999). It is defined as the ability to recognize, categorize, and draw upon features of the natural environment—flora, fauna, geological formations, and weather patterns. The student's ability to classify species and understand ecosystems is the hallmark of this intelligence. Logical-Mathematical intelligence involves abstract reasoning and numbers; Spatial involves mental visualization; Bodily-Kinesthetic involves skilled use of the body.

questions.text: As per the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) 2005 and the Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE) guidelines, a teacher uses class discussions, portfolio reviews, and anecdotal records primarily to identify specific learning difficulties of students and immediately adapt her teaching strategies. This purpose of assessment is technically termed as:
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Distinguish 'FOR' vs 'OF'. "Identify difficulties" + "Adapt teaching" + "During instruction" = Formative purpose = Assessment FOR Learning. 'Assessment OF Learning' is summative (end-term, grading, ranking). 'Assessment AS Learning' focuses on student self-monitoring. 'Placement Assessment' is pre-instruction (entry behavior). Eliminate A, C, D by timing and purpose. Full Solution: NCF 2005 emphasizes a shift from 'Assessment of Learning' (summative, judgmental) to 'Assessment for Learning' (formative, diagnostic). Assessment for Learning occurs during the teaching-learning process. Its core function is to provide feedback to the teacher about student progress, diagnose learning gaps, and inform immediate pedagogical modifications. Tools like anecdotal records, portfolios, and observations are classic formative tools. Assessment as Learning involves student metacognition/self-assessment. Placement assessment happens before instruction begins.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
questions.solution: Shortcut: A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9. For 12348, digit sum = 1+2+3+4+8 = 18, which is divisible by 9. The other options have digit sums 21, 24, and 26 respectively, none of which are multiples of 9. Therefore, 12348 is the only number divisible by 9.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of 7^23?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Divide the exponent 23 by 4; remainder = 3. The third digit in the cycle is 3. Step‑by‑step: 7^1=7, 7^2=49→9, 7^3=343→3, 7^4=2401→1, cycle repeats. Since 23 = 4×5 + 3, the unit digit equals that of 7^3, which is 3.

questions.text: A shirt's price is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the price?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For an x% increase followed by an x% decrease, net change = -x^2/100 %. Here x=20, so net = -400/100 = -4% (a 4% decrease). Step‑by‑step: Let original price = 100. After 20% increase → 120. Then 20% decrease on 120 → 120 - 24 = 96. Final price 96, which is 4% less than original 100.

questions.text: A Class V EVS teacher asks students to maintain a 'Learning Diary' where they record what they found easy, difficult, and the strategies they used to solve a problem on 'Water Scarcity'. The teacher reviews these diaries to help students reflect on their own thinking processes. This practice aligns with which purpose of assessment?

options.label: B
options.text: Assessment for Learning (Formative - Teacher driven adjustment)

questions.solution: Shortcut: Keywords 'students record', 'reflect on their own thinking', and 'strategies they used' indicate metacognition and self-regulation by the learner. This is the definition of Assessment as Learning. Eliminate 'of Learning' (grading), 'for Learning' (teacher adjusts teaching), and 'Diagnostic' (pre-teaching). Step-by-step: Assessment of Learning is summative certification. Assessment for Learning is formative where teachers use evidence to adjust instruction. Assessment as Learning focuses on students self-assessing, monitoring progress, and reflecting on their learning process (metacognition). Diagnostic assessment identifies prior knowledge/misconceptions before teaching. The stem describes students actively reflecting on their cognitive processes via a diary, fitting Assessment as Learning.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of 'Nutrient - Primary Function in Human Body' is correctly matched?

options.label: A
options.text: Vitamin C - Strengthening bones and teeth

options.label: B
options.text: Iron - Formation of haemoglobin in red blood cells

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use elimination by matching known deficiency/function pairs. Vitamin C → Immunity/Collagen (Bones=Calcium). Calcium → Bones/Teeth (Night Blindness=Vitamin A). Fibre → Digestion/Roughage (Energy=Carbs/Fats). Only Iron → Haemoglobin remains correct. Step-by-step: Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy; it aids collagen synthesis, not bone mineralization (Calcium’s role). Calcium deficiency causes Rickets/Osteoporosis; Night Blindness is caused by Vitamin A deficiency. Dietary Fibre is indigestible cellulose providing zero calories; it adds bulk for egestion. Iron is the central atom in the haem molecule of haemoglobin, essential for oxygen transport; deficiency causes Anaemia. Option B is the only scientifically accurate match.

questions.text: In the context of traditional water conservation methods in India, which of the following structures is a 'Stepwell' typically found in the arid regions of Gujarat and Rajasthan, designed to access groundwater and serve as a community gathering space?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Map structure name to Region/Type. 'Stepwell' + 'Gujarat/Rajasthan' → Baoli/Vav. Johad = Earthen check dam (Rajasthan). Eri/Kere = Tank systems (Tamil Nadu/Karnataka). Step-by-step: Traditional water harvesting is region-specific. Stepwells (Baolis in North, Vavs in Gujarat) are multi-storeyed subterranean structures with steps descending to the water table, prominent in arid Gujarat (e.g., Rani ki Vav) and Rajasthan. Johads are small earthen check dams capturing monsoon runoff (Alwar, Rajasthan). Eris (Tamil Nadu) and Keres (Karnataka) are ancient tank/cascade systems for surface water storage in peninsular India. The description of a stepwell accessing groundwater in Gujarat/Rajasthan matches Baoli/Vav.
questions.topic: Social Studies Content - Water Conservation (Traditional Methods)

questions.text: A Class III teacher encourages students to work in groups to create a story. She provides word cards and sentence starters, gradually withdrawing support as students become confident in constructing sentences independently. This strategy is most aligned with which concept proposed by Lev Vygotsky?

options.label: B
options.text: Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and Scaffolding

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Option A (Chomsky's Innatist theory), Option C (Skinner's Behaviorist theory), and Option D (Piaget's Cognitive stages) as they do not emphasize social interaction and temporary, adjustable teacher support. Option B directly matches the description of 'gradual withdrawal of support'. Full Solution: Lev Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) is the gap between what a learner can do independently and what they can achieve with guidance. Scaffolding is the temporary support (word cards, starters) provided by the teacher within this zone, which is progressively removed as the learner internalizes the skill.
questions.topic: Language Pedagogy - Theories of Language Learning

questions.text: Choose the sentence in which the verb agrees correctly with the subject.

options.label: A
options.text: A number of students has failed to submit the assignment.

options.label: B
options.text: Neither the principal nor the teachers is attending the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: The furniture in the classroom were old and broken.

options.label: D
options.text: The committee are divided in their opinion on the new syllabus.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply SVA rules to eliminate errors rapidly. 'Furniture' is a singular collective noun -> takes 'was' (Eliminate C). 'A number of' means 'many' -> takes plural verb 'have' (Eliminate A). 'Neither...Nor' follows Proximity Rule -> verb agrees with nearest subject 'teachers' (plural) -> 'are' (Eliminate B). 'Committee' acting as individuals (divided opinion) correctly takes plural verb 'are' (Option D correct). Full Solution: Collective nouns take plural verbs when members act individually ('committee are divided'). 'A number of' requires a plural verb ('have failed'). In correlative conjunctions 'Neither...Nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it ('teachers are'). 'Furniture' is uncountable and always singular ('was').

questions.text: Read the sentence: 'The school management decided to call off the annual sports day due to the sudden spell of heavy rain.' Which option best expresses the meaning of the phrasal verb 'call off' as used in the sentence?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use context clues ('due to heavy rain') to eliminate illogical options. 'Organize hurriedly' (B) and 'Announce publicly' (D) contradict the context of stopping an event. Distinguish 'Call off' (Cancel) from 'Put off' (Postpone). Sudden severe weather usually forces cancellation, not mere delay. Option C is correct. Full Solution: 'Call off' is an inseparable phrasal verb meaning to cancel a planned event. 'Put off' means to postpone. The causal phrase 'due to the sudden spell of heavy rain' implies the event cannot proceed, making 'Cancel completely' the precise semantic fit.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the past perfect tense.

options.label: A
options.text: By the time we arrived, the train left.

options.label: B
options.text: By the time we arrived, the train had left.

options.label: C
options.text: By the time we arrive, the train had left.

options.label: D
options.text: By the time we arrived, the train has left.

questions.solution: Shortcut: In a 'by the time' clause referring to the past, the earlier action must be in past perfect (had + V3). Only option B uses 'had left'. Full solution: The main clause 'we arrived' is simple past, so the action completed before that requires past perfect. Options A, C, D use simple past, present, or present perfect, which are incorrect.

questions.text: Select the word most opposite in meaning to "benevolent".
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the antonym by eliminating synonyms. 'Kind', 'generous', 'compassionate' are synonyms of benevolent; only 'malevolent' means ill‑wishing. Full solution: Benevolent = showing kindness; its opposite is malevolent = wishing harm. The other three options share the positive connotation, so they are eliminated.

questions.text: According to NCF 2005, the teacher's role in a language classroom is best described as:
questions.solution: Shortcut: NCF 2005 advocates a constructivist, child‑centred pedagogy where the teacher facilitates rather than transmits. Options A, B, D describe traditional or limited roles. Full solution: The framework positions the teacher as a facilitator who creates learning environments, guides inquiry, and supports learner autonomy, making C the correct choice.

questions.text: A shopkeeper in a local market marks his goods 40% above the cost price. He announces a discount of 10% but mistakenly calculates the discount on the cost price instead of the marked price. What is his actual profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let CP = ₹100.
MP = ₹140 (40% above CP).
Discount = 10% of CP = ₹10.
SP = MP – Discount = ₹140 – ₹10 = ₹130.
Profit = SP – CP = ₹30.
Profit% = (30/100)×100 = 30%.

questions.text: A village panchayat has ₹ 12,600 for a community festival. It first sets aside ₹ 600 for an emergency fund. The remaining amount is divided among three committees in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much does the second committee receive?
questions.solution:
1. Total amount = ₹12,600.
2. Emergency fund = ₹600.
3. Remaining = 12,600 - 600 = ₹12,000.
4. Ratio parts = 3+4+5 = 12.
5. Value per part = 12,000 / 12 = ₹1,000.
6. Second committee share = 4 × 1,000 = ₹4,000.

questions.text: A dairy farmer has a 60‑litre mixture of milk and water in the ratio 7:5. He removes 12 litres of the mixture and replaces it with pure milk. Later, he removes 10 litres of the new mixture and replaces it with pure water. What is the final ratio of milk to water?
questions.solution:
Initial: milk = 60×7/12 = 35 L, water = 25 L.
After 1st removal (12 L): milk removed = 12×7/12 = 7 L, water removed = 5 L → milk = 28 L, water = 20 L.
Add 12 L milk → milk = 40 L, water = 20 L (ratio 2:1).
After 2nd removal (10 L): milk removed = 10×2/3 = 20/3 L, water removed = 10/3 L → milk = 100/3 L, water = 50/3 L.
Add 10 L water → water = 80/3 L.
Final ratio = (100/3) : (80/3) = 5:4.

questions.text: A construction project requires a total of 5,000 man‑hours. Three workers are hired initially. For the first 4 days each works 8 hours per day and is paid Rs 120 per hour. After that, for the next 3 days the same three workers work 10 hours per day, and their hourly wage is increased by 15 %. From the 8th day onward a supervisor adds two more workers, so that five workers now work 8 hours each day until the remaining man‑hours are completed. Assuming the original hourly rate (Rs 120) applies to the additional workers and to the original three workers after the overtime period, what is the total amount paid to all workers at the end of the project?
questions.solution:
1. First 4 days: 3 workers × 8 hrs × 4 days = 96 hrs. Cost = 96 × 120 = Rs 11,520.
2. Next 3 days: 3 workers × 10 hrs × 3 days = 90 hrs. New rate = 120 × 1.15 = Rs 138. Cost = 90 × 138 = Rs 12,420.
3. Hours done so far = 96 + 90 = 186 hrs; cost so far = 11,520 + 12,420 = Rs 23,940.
4. Remaining hours = 5,000 − 186 = 4,814 hrs.
5. From day 8 onward 5 workers work 8 hrs/day → 40 hrs per day. Total cost for remaining hours at original rate: 4,814 hrs × 120 = Rs 577,680.
6. Total payment = 23,940 + 577,680 = Rs 601,620.
Thus option A is correct.

questions.text: A vendor purchases 120 kg of mangoes at Rs 30 per kg. He immediately sells 40 kg at Rs 45 per kg. He then buys an additional 50 kg of mangoes at Rs 28 per kg. The remaining mangoes are sold in two batches: 70 kg at Rs 42 per kg and the rest at Rs 38 per kg. What is the overall profit percentage (to one decimal place) on his total expenditure?
questions.solution:
1. Initial cost =120×30=Rs 3600.
2. Revenue from first sale =40×45=Rs 1800.
3. Additional purchase cost =50×28=Rs 1400; total cost=3600+1400=Rs 5000.
4. Revenue from second batch =70×42=Rs 2940.
5. Remaining mangoes =130‑70=60 kg; revenue =60×38=Rs 2280.
6. Total revenue =1800+2940+2280=Rs 7020.
7. Profit =7020‑5000=Rs 2020.
8. Profit % =2020/5000×100=40.4%.
questions.style: Layered Replacement with Variable Base Profit

questions.text:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error:

The committee, along with its members, are meeting tomorrow to discuss the budget.
questions.solution: The subject is ‘The committee’ (singular). The phrase ‘along with its members’ is an intervening phrase and does not affect the verb. Hence the verb must be singular ‘is meeting’. The error lies in part C.

questions.text: After the sudden policy reversal, the director decided to ______ the initiative, realizing that further investment would be futile.
questions.solution:
1. The context indicates stopping a project because it is no longer viable.
2. "Pull the plug" is the idiom meaning to discontinue or terminate something.
3. The other options mean: manipulate (pull the strings), deceive (pull the wool), or initiate action (pull the trigger).
4. Only "pull the plug" matches the required meaning.

questions.text:
Select the pronoun that correctly completes the sentence:

The batsman scored more runs in the innings than ______.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify the elliptical clause after 'than' – the full comparison is 'than he scored'.
Step 2: The omitted verb 'scored' needs a subject pronoun.
Step 3: 'he' is the subject form; 'him' is object, 'his' possessive, 'himself' reflexive.
Therefore 'he' is the only grammatically correct choice.

questions.text: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana seeks to ______ the financial distress caused by crop failure among smallholder farmers.
questions.solution: 1. Identify the object noun phrase: 'financial distress'. 2. Recall standard collocations: 'alleviate distress' is a fixed formal collocation; 'mitigate' pairs with 'risk/impact'; 'reduce/lessen' are generic and less idiomatic in official documents. 3. Choose the verb that both fits the meaning and matches the formal register of a government scheme. Hence 'alleviate' is correct.

questions.text: The ______ of the scheme was ______ by the villagers, who praised its timely disbursement but questioned its long‑term sustainability.
questions.solution:
1. First blank needs a noun for the scheme's result; all four nouns are possible.
2. Second blank requires a passive‑voice verb showing villagers' reaction.
3. Only "welcomed" collocates naturally with "impact" in this register.
4. Other pairs are either unidiomatic or carry negative connotation.
questions.topic: Vocabulary in Context - Dual Register Cloze

questions.text: The new agricultural scheme was launched with much fanfare; ______, the uptake among smallholders remained low. Experts attribute this ______ to the complex documentation process.
questions.solution: 1. The first sentence presents a contrast between fanfare and low uptake, so the blank needs a contrastive conjunctive adverb (however/nevertheless). 2. The second sentence refers to the low uptake with "this", requiring a noun denoting unwillingness (reluctance/hesitation/apathy). 3. Only option A supplies a contrast connector (however) and a fitting noun (reluctance). 4. Options B, C use wrong logical connectors; D uses a contrast connector but an incompatible noun (eagerness).

questions.text: A retailer first raises the marked price of a product by 20% and then offers a discount of 15% on the increased price. What is the net percentage change in the selling price of the product with respect to its original marked price?
questions.solution: 1. Original price = 100 (assume). 2. After 20% rise: 100 × 1.20 = 120. 3. Discount of 15% on 120: 120 × (1‑0.15) = 120 × 0.85 = 102. 4. Final price = 102, which is 2% higher than 100. Hence net change = 2% increase.

questions.text: The new railway safety protocol is ______ to reduce accidents, even though it is not impossible that the initial rollout will encounter delays.
questions.solution:
1. The phrase "not impossible" is a double negative meaning "possible".
2. The concession clause "even though it is not impossible that..." acknowledges a potential hurdle but does not negate the main expectation.
3. The main clause requires a word showing anticipation of a positive outcome.
4. "expected" conveys that the protocol is anticipated to reduce accidents.
5. "unlikely" and "doubtful" contradict the positive sense; "certain" overstates the certainty.
6. Therefore, "expected" is the only word that fits both the grammar and the logical polarity.

questions.text: A merchant has 500 L of a solution containing 8% salt. He removes 50 L of the mixture and replaces it with water. Then he adds 30 L of a 20% salt solution. After that, he removes 40 L of the resulting mixture and again replaces it with water. What is the final percentage of salt in the solution (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
1. Initial salt = 0.08×500 = 40 kg.
2. Remove 50 L: salt removed = 40×50/500 = 4 kg → remaining salt = 36 kg, volume = 450 L; add 50 L water → volume = 500 L.
3. Add 30 L of 20% solution: salt added = 0.20×30 = 6 kg → salt = 42 kg, volume = 530 L.
4. Remove 40 L: salt removed = 42×40/530 ≈ 3.169 kg → remaining salt ≈ 38.831 kg, volume = 490 L; add 40 L water → volume = 530 L.
5. Final % salt = (38.831/530)×100 ≈ 7.33%.

questions.text: A factory initially employs 10 workers who together produce 200 widgets per day. After 5 days, 2 workers leave and the remaining workers increase their individual efficiency by 20%. After another 3 days, 3 new workers join, each having 80% of the original per‑worker efficiency. Simultaneously, a machine runs throughout the 12‑day period producing 50 widgets per day, but it breaks down for the 7th and 8th days. What is the total number of widgets produced by the factory in the 12 days?
With the monsoon arriving early, the farmers decided to ______ and harvest their crops before the rains damaged them.

options.label: A
options.text: make hay while the sun shines

options.label: D
options.text: hit the nail on the head

questions.solution:
1. Context shows urgency to act before rain arrives.
2. Required meaning: take advantage of a brief favorable period.
3. 'make hay while the sun shines' exactly conveys this.
4. Other idioms mean: face difficulty, work late, be precise — none fit.

questions.text: In the following sentence, one word is a homophone error. Identify the incorrect word: "The artist drew a beautiful scene on the canvas, using a pallet of vibrant colors."
questions.solution:
1. Spot the homophone pair: pallet (wooden platform) vs palette (range of colours).
2. Context "vibrant colors" demands "palette".
3. The sentence uses "pallet", which is wrong.
4. Hence the incorrect word is "pallet".

questions.text: The scheme was well-funded; ______ it failed to meet its targets.
questions.solution:
1. The first clause states a positive fact (well-funded), the second a negative outcome (failed) → contrast needed.
2. A semicolon before the blank requires a conjunctive adverb (transition word) followed by a comma.
3. Among options, "however", "therefore", "moreover" are conjunctive adverbs; "yet" is a coordinating conjunction.
4. "therefore" and "moreover" show result/addition, not contrast.
5. "however" signals contrast and fits the punctuation rule.
6. Therefore, "however" is the only correct choice.

questions.text: The new railway electrification project was sanctioned in 2022; nevertheless, the ______ of funds delayed its completion by two years.
questions.solution:
1. The connector "nevertheless" introduces a contrast to the first clause.
2. First clause: project sanctioned (positive step).
3. Second clause must give a negative reason for the delay.
4. "Shortage" means a lack, fitting the negative context.
5. "Disbursement" and "allocation" are neutral/positive actions; "surplus" is opposite.
6. Therefore, "shortage" is the only word that logically completes the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage, the writer describes the impact of a new railway line on a remote village. Choose the word that best replaces the underlined word so that the meaning of the sentence remains unchanged.

"The inauguration of the line has been a **panacea** for the villagers, eradicating the long‑standing problem of isolation and opening avenues for trade and education."

Options:
questions.solution: 1. Identify meaning of 'panacea' – a solution or cure for all problems. 2. The sentence says the railway is a panacea, i.e., it solves the problem. 3. Look for a synonym that fits the same meaning. 4. 'Cure' means a remedy that eliminates a disease/problem, matching the context. 5. 'Remedy' and 'antidote' are close but imply treatment rather than a complete solution; 'bane' is opposite. 6. Therefore the correct replacement is 'cure'.

questions.text:
In the following pair of sentences, the first sentence contains a word used in an incorrect form. Identify the correct form of that word which can also appropriately fill the blank in the second sentence.
Sentence 1: The committee's *implement* of the new policy was delayed due to procedural hurdles.
Sentence 2: The ______ of the policy will be reviewed next month.
questions.solution:
1. In Sentence 1, 'implement' is a verb (or a noun meaning a tool) but the context requires a noun denoting the process of putting a policy into effect.
2. The appropriate noun form is obtained by adding the suffix '-ation' to the verb 'implement', giving 'implementation'.
3. 'Implementation' fits grammatically as the subject of Sentence 2 and conveys the intended meaning of 'the process of executing the policy'.
4. The other options are either a present participle ('implementing'), the base verb ('implement'), or an adjective ('implemental'), none of which function as a noun denoting the process.
questions.style: Verb-to-Noun Conversion Cloze with Error Detection

questions.text: According to Jean Piaget, a 4-year-old child watches an adult pour water from a short, wide glass into a tall, thin glass. The child insists the tall glass has 'more water' because the water level is higher. This error demonstrates the child's inability to decentre and focus on only one dimension (height) while ignoring the other (width). What is the specific term Piaget used for this cognitive limitation?
questions.solution: Centration is the tendency to focus on only one salient aspect of a situation (e.g., height of water) while ignoring other relevant aspects (e.g., width of glass). Egocentrism refers to the inability to take another's perspective (tested via Three Mountains task). Irreversibility is the inability to mentally reverse an action. Animism is attributing life to inanimate objects. Shortcut: Eliminate Egocentrism (perspective taking), Irreversibility (mental reversal), and Animism (life attribution); the scenario describes focusing on a single dimension.

questions.text: A 13-year-old student decides not to cheat on an exam because they believe 'cheating is unfair to other students who studied hard, and I want to be seen as a trustworthy person by my friends and teachers.' According to Lawrence Kohlberg's theory of moral development, this reasoning aligns with which specific stage?

options.label: A
options.text: A. Stage 1: Obedience and Punishment Orientation

questions.solution: Stage 3 (Good Interpersonal Relationships) is characterized by reasoning based on social approval, trust, loyalty, and concern for others' feelings ('good boy/good girl' orientation). Stage 1 focuses on avoiding punishment. Stage 2 focuses on self-interest and fair deals. Stage 4 focuses on law, duty, and social order maintenance. Shortcut: Keywords 'unfair to others', 'trustworthy', 'seen by friends/teachers' indicate interpersonal concordance (Stage 3), not law/order (Stage 4) or punishment (Stage 1).

questions.text: Jerome Bruner proposed that intellectual development moves through three modes of representation. A teacher uses physical beads and strings to teach addition to Class I students, then shifts to pictures of beads on a worksheet for Class II, and finally introduces the abstract symbols '+' and '=' in Class III. This progression follows which specific sequence of Bruner's modes?
questions.solution: Bruner's sequence is Enactive (action-based, manipulating objects), Iconic (image-based, visual representations), and Symbolic (language/abstract symbols). The scenario moves from beads (Enactive) to pictures (Iconic) to symbols (Symbolic). Shortcut: Remember the acronym 'E-I-S' (Enactive-Iconic-Symbolic) matching the natural progression from concrete doing to abstract thinking. Option D is the only one starting with Enactive and ending with Symbolic.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the number obtained from the expression (7^95)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The unit digits of powers of 7 follow a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Divide the exponent 95 by 4; the remainder is 3. The 3rd value in the cycle (7→9→3) is 3. Full Solution: Cyclicity of 7 is 4 (7^1=7, 7^2=49, 7^3=343, 7^4=2401). 95 = 4×23 + 3. Unit digit of 7^95 = Unit digit of (7^4)^23 × 7^3 = 1 × 343 = 3.

questions.text: A Class III student recognizes a square by its appearance as a 'box shape' but cannot list its properties like 'all sides equal' or 'all angles 90 degrees'. According to Van Hiele's levels of geometric thought, this student is operating at which level?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Memorize the sequence: Level 0 (Visualization - recognizes by whole appearance/look), Level 1 (Analysis - identifies properties), Level 2 (Informal Deduction - understands relationships between properties/classes), Level 3 (Deduction - constructs proofs). The child relies solely on visual look, so it is Level 0. Full Solution: Van Hiele Level 0 (Visualization) is characterized by identifying shapes based on global visual impression (e.g., 'it looks like a door') rather than by defining geometric properties. Since the student cannot articulate properties, they have not reached Level 1 (Analysis).
questions.topic: Pedagogy - Van Hiele Levels of Geometric Thinking

questions.text: A train 150 metres long is running at a speed of 60 km/h. In what time will it cross a telegraph post?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Convert speed km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18 (60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s). Time = Distance / Speed = 150 / (50/3) = 150 × 3/50 = 9 seconds. Option elimination: 60 km/h ≈ 16.67 m/s; 150/16.67 ≈ 9. Full Solution: Speed = 60 km/h = 60 × (5/18) m/s = 50/3 m/s. Distance to cover = Length of train = 150 m. Time = Distance / Speed = 150 / (50/3) = 150 × 3/50 = 9 seconds.

questions.text: As per the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) 2005, the subject 'Environmental Studies' (EVS) at the primary stage (Classes I–II) is structured around the child's immediate environment. Which of the following statements accurately reflects the curricular approach for EVS at this stage according to NCF 2005?

options.label: A
options.text: EVS is taught as separate Science and Social Science textbooks from Class I onwards to build disciplinary rigour early.

options.label: B
options.text: EVS is presented as an integrated curricular area drawing upon Science, Social Science, and Environmental Education concepts without rigid subject boundaries.

options.label: C
options.text: The focus is exclusively on natural environment components like plants, animals, and weather, delaying social environment themes until Class III.

options.label: D
options.text: Textbooks are avoided completely; the entire curriculum is transacted only through unstructured outdoor play and storytelling.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options suggesting 'separate subjects' (A), 'exclusive natural focus' (C), or 'no textbooks' (D) as NCF 2005 emphasizes integration, holistic environment (natural + social), and contextual materials. Worked Solution: NCF 2005 positions EVS (Classes I–II) as an integrated area combining insights from Science, Social Science, and Environmental Education. It focuses on the child's immediate environment (both natural and social) using themes like Family, Food, Water, Shelter, and Travel. It does not separate disciplines, exclude social themes, or discard textbooks.

questions.text: A grandmother prepares mango pickle (Aam ka Achar) using raw mangoes, salt, turmeric, mustard oil, and spices. The pickle remains edible for over a year without refrigeration. Which scientific principle primarily explains the preservation of this pickle?

options.label: A
options.text: Low temperature inhibits enzymatic reactions and microbial metabolism.

options.label: B
options.text: High concentration of salt and oil creates a hypertonic environment causing plasmolysis of microbial cells and anaerobic conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Turmeric and spices act as antibiotics that sterilize the food matrix completely.

options.label: D
options.text: The acidic pH of raw mangoes denatures all proteins, preventing spoilage indefinitely.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate modern methods (A - refrigeration), absolute claims (C - 'sterilize completely', D - 'indefinitely'). Traditional pickling uses osmosis (salt) and anaerobic barrier (oil). Worked Solution: Pickling preserves food primarily through high osmotic pressure created by salt (and sugar), which draws water out of microbial cells via plasmolysis, inhibiting their growth. The layer of oil creates an anaerobic seal, further preventing aerobic spoilage. While acidity (mango/turmeric) helps, the primary preservative mechanism in oil-based Indian pickles is the hypertonic environment and oxygen exclusion.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the modes of transport used by 100 students of Class V to reach school, which mode of transport is used by the maximum number of students? | Mode of Transport | Number of Students | | :--- | :--- | | School Bus | 35 | | Bicycle | 20 | | Walking | 25 | | Private Car/Van | 10 | | Public Bus/Metro | 10 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Number of Students' column for the highest value (35) and map it to the corresponding 'Mode of Transport' (School Bus). Worked Solution: The table lists frequencies for five categories. Comparing the values: School Bus (35) > Walking (25) > Bicycle (20) > Private Car/Van (10) = Public Bus/Metro (10). The maximum frequency is 35, corresponding to School Bus.

questions.text: According to the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) 2005, what is the recommended pedagogical stance towards the multilingual nature of the Indian classroom?

options.label: A
options.text: It should be discouraged to ensure uniformity in the medium of instruction.

options.label: B
options.text: It should be treated as a resource and a pedagogical strategy for language learning.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a major obstacle to learning the standard language and requires remedial drill.

options.label: D
options.text: It is irrelevant at the primary stage as children acquire language naturally without intervention.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options with negative views on multilingualism (A, C, D). NCF 2005 explicitly frames linguistic diversity as an asset. Worked: The NCF 2005 Position Paper on 'Teaching of Indian Languages' states that multilingualism should be used as a resource, classroom strategy, and a goal to promote cognitive flexibility and respect for diversity. Option B accurately reflects this mandate.

questions.text: Identify the sentence with the correct subject-verb agreement.

options.label: A
options.text: One of my friends who are coming to the party live in Delhi.

options.label: B
options.text: One of my friends who is coming to the party lives in Delhi.

options.label: C
options.text: One of my friends who are coming to the party lives in Delhi.

options.label: D
options.text: One of my friends who is coming to the party live in Delhi.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Split the structure. Main subject 'One' (Singular) -> Verb 'lives'. Relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'friends' (Plural) -> Verb 'are'. Eliminate A, D (main verb plural) and B (relative verb singular). Worked: In 'One of my friends who...', the main clause subject is 'One', requiring singular verb 'lives'. The relative clause 'who are coming' modifies 'friends' (plural antecedent), requiring plural verb 'are'. Only Option C satisfies both rules: 'One... lives' and 'friends who are'.

questions.text: Choose the option that correctly identifies the error in the following sentence: "If the teacher would have explained the concept again, the students would have understood it better."

options.label: A
options.text: Error in "would have explained" (Should be "had explained")

questions.solution: Shortcut: Third Conditional Rule: 'If' clause never takes 'would have'; it takes 'had + V3'. Eliminate B, C, D immediately. Worked: This is a Type 3 Conditional (unreal past). The structure is: If + Past Perfect (had + V3), ... would have + V3. The error lies in the 'If' clause using 'would have explained' instead of 'had explained'. The main clause 'would have understood' is correctly formed.

questions.text: Choose the appropriate article to fill in the blank: He is ___ MLA from our constituency.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Focus on the sound of the word following the article, not its spelling. 'MLA' is pronounced /ˌemˌelˈeɪ/, starting with a vowel sound /e/, so the indefinite article 'an' is required. Full solution: The abbreviation MLA is read letter by letter; the first letter 'M' produces a vowel sound /em/. Therefore 'an' is used before vowel sounds, while 'a' is used before consonant sounds. 'The' would make it definite, and a singular countable noun like 'MLA' cannot stand without a determiner.

questions.text: Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the phrasal verb 'called off' in the sentence: The match was called off due to bad weather.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate each phrasal verb with its distinct meaning: 'call off' = cancel, 'put off' = postpone. Eliminate 'started' and 'announced' as they are unrelated. Full solution: The phrasal verb 'call off' means to cancel an event that was planned. 'Postponed' corresponds to 'put off', not 'call off'. The other options do not convey the meaning of cancellation. Hence 'cancelled' is the correct choice.

questions.text: Choose the correct modal phrase to complete the sentence: You ___ come to the office tomorrow; the meeting has been cancelled.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Determine the logical relationship: the meeting is cancelled, so there is no obligation. 'Need not' expresses absence of necessity, while 'must not' expresses prohibition. Full solution: The context indicates that coming to the office is not required. 'Need not' correctly shows that the action is unnecessary. 'Must not' would forbid the action, 'should not' advises against it, and 'cannot' denotes inability. Therefore, 'need not' is the appropriate modal phrase.

questions.text: A car covers a distance of 120 km at a speed of 60 km/h. If the speed is increased by 20%, by what percentage does the travel time decrease?
questions.solution: Original time = 120/60 = 2 h. New speed = 60 × 1.20 = 72 km/h. New time = 120/72 = 5/3 h. Decrease = 2 − 5/3 = 1/3 h. % decrease = (1/3 ÷ 2) × 100 = 100/6 = 16 2/3%.

questions.text: A retail store advertises a 10% discount on the marked price of a television. After this discount is applied, the store offers an additional 5% off on the already reduced price. What is the overall percentage discount on the original marked price?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price be 100 units.
First discount: 10% of 100 = 10 → price = 100‑10 = 90.
Second discount: 5% of 90 = 4.5 → price = 90‑4.5 = 85.5.
Total discount = 100‑85.5 = 14.5 units.
Hence overall discount = 14.5% of the original price.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 25% above cost price. He uses a faulty weight of 900 grams for 1 kg and offers a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let CP per kg = ₹100.
MP = 125 (25% markup).
He sells 900 g as 1 kg at 10% discount → SP for 900 g = 125 × 0.9 = ₹112.5.
Cost of 900 g = ₹90.
Profit = 112.5 – 90 = ₹22.5.
Profit% = (22.5/90)×100 = 25%.

questions.text: A milk vendor has a 200-litre tank containing milk with 30% fat. Every hour he removes a certain percentage of the mixture and replaces it with milk having 10% fat. In the first hour he removes 20%, in the second hour 25%, and in the third hour 30%. What is the fat percentage in the tank after three hours?
questions.solution:
Initial fat = 30% of 200 = 60 L.
Hour1: Remove 20% (40 L) → fat removed = 12 L; remaining fat = 48 L. Add 40 L of 10% fat → +4 L fat = 52 L (26%).
Hour2: Remove 25% (50 L) of 26% → fat removed = 13 L; remaining fat = 39 L. Add 50 L of 10% → +5 L = 44 L (22%).
Hour3: Remove 30% (60 L) of 22% → fat removed = 13.2 L; remaining fat = 30.8 L. Add 60 L of 10% → +6 L = 36.8 L. Final fat% = 36.8/200 = 18.4%.

questions.text: A contractor undertakes a project to be completed in 20 days. He starts with 20 men and 30 women. The efficiency of a man is twice that of a woman. After 10 days, 5 men leave and 10 women join. After another 5 days, 5 men join and 5 women leave. The work finishes exactly on the 20th day. The total wages paid to all workers is ₹1,42,500, distributed in proportion to the work done by each worker. What is the daily wage of a woman?
questions.solution:
Let woman's 1 day work = 1 unit, man's = 2 units.
Phase1 (10 days): Men=20*2*10=400, Women=30*1*10=300.
Phase2 (5 days): Men=15*2*5=150, Women=40*1*5=200.
Phase3 (5 days): Men=20*2*5=200, Women=35*1*5=175.
Total work=400+300+150+200+200+175=1425 units.
Wage per unit=142500/1425=100.
Woman's daily wage=1*100=₹100.
questions.style: Proportional Wage Distribution with Workforce Change

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition to complete the idiom in the following sentence: After the long journey, he felt ______ the weather.
questions.solution: The idiom 'under the weather' means feeling unwell. Only 'under' fits the fixed expression; other prepositions break the idiom.

questions.text:
The following sentence has four underlined parts labelled (A), (B), (C) and (D). One of these parts contains an error in parallel structure. Identify the part that contains the error.
Sentence: The new scheme aims to (A) improve rural connectivity, (B) enhance digital literacy, (C) and providing healthcare access, (D) across the region.
questions.solution:
1. The phrase "aims to" introduces a list of infinitives.
2. Parallelism requires each item to be in the base verb form: improve, enhance, provide.
3. Part (C) uses "providing" (gerund) instead of "provide", breaking the pattern.
4. Hence the error lies in part (C).
questions.style: Parallelism Violation Detection in Infinitive List

questions.text: The Ministry of Rural Development has decided to ______ the new digital payment module for the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) across all gram panchayats by March 2026.
questions.solution:
1. The sentence describes a ministry launching a digital module for a national scheme — a formal administrative rollout.
2. In official Indian government communications, the verb used for putting a system into active use is “operationalize”.
3. “Implement” and “execute” are generic; “administer” means to manage, not to launch.
4. Therefore the register‑appropriate choice is “operationalize”.

questions.text: The sudden announcement of a flash sale on the e‑commerce platform triggered a ______ of traffic, causing the servers to crash within minutes. (Choose the word that means ‘a sudden, brief increase’ and collocates naturally with ‘of traffic’.)
questions.solution:
1. The clue asks for a word meaning ‘a sudden, brief increase’.
2. ‘Surge’ fits this meaning exactly and forms the standard collocation ‘surge of traffic’.
3. ‘Trickle’ and ‘drizzle’ denote a slow, small flow – opposite of the required sense.
4. ‘Deluge’ means a large overwhelming amount but lacks the ‘brief’ nuance and is less idiomatic with ‘traffic’.
5. Therefore, ‘surge’ is the only option satisfying both definition and collocation.

questions.text: The committee's final report was anything but ______, since the evidence presented directly contradicted its findings.
questions.solution:
1. Identify "anything but" as a negative polarity phrase meaning "definitely not".
2. The "since" clause states evidence contradicted the findings, so the report was not accurate.
3. Therefore the blank must be the positive quality denied: "accurate".
4. Option "inaccurate" would reverse the meaning ("not inaccurate" = accurate), clashing with the context.
5. "Biased" and "comprehensive" do not create the required logical contrast.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, a segment is underlined. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct and logically coherent.

Because the new policy was implemented last month, the complaints have not decreased, and the department is considering to revise it.

options.label: A
options.text: Although the new policy was implemented last month, the complaints have not decreased, and the department is considering revising it.

options.label: B
options.text: Because the new policy was implemented last month, the complaints have not decreased, and the department is considering to revise it.

options.label: C
options.text: Since the new policy had been implemented last month, the complaints have not decreased, and the department is considering revising it.

options.label: D
options.text: While the new policy was implemented last month, the complaints have not decreased, and the department is considering to revise it.

questions.solution: 1. The context shows a contrast: policy implemented but complaints persist → need a contrastive connector (Although). 2. After "considering" the gerund form is required → "revising" not "to revise". 3. Option A satisfies both; B wrong connector & verb; C wrong tense (had been) & connector; D connector "While" less appropriate & verb error.

questions.text: In the fund‑management protocol of a centrally sponsored scheme, the prescribed sequence of stages is: sanction → release → utilization → ______. The missing stage must be the formal term used in government accounting for the final reconciliation of accounts.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the lexical chain: sanction, release, utilization are successive fund‑management steps.
2. The next logical step in government accounting is the formal reconciliation called “settlement”.
3. “Payment” duplicates release; “clearance” precedes release; “completion” is generic, not a technical term.
4. Only “settlement” satisfies both chain continuation and formal register.
5. Hence the correct fill is “settlement”.

questions.text: A tea vendor mixes 3 kg of Type A tea costing Rs 120 per kg with 2 kg of Type B tea costing Rs 150 per kg. He sells half of this mixture at a 10 % profit on its cost. He then adds 1 kg of Type C tea costing Rs 180 per kg to the remaining mixture and sells the rest at the same selling price per kg as used for the first half. What is the overall profit percentage on the whole transaction (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
1. Initial cost =3×120+2×150=660 Rs; total qty=5 kg; cost/kg=660/5=132 Rs.
2. 10 % profit ⇒ selling price/kg for first half =132×1.10=145.2 Rs.
3. Revenue from first half (2.5 kg)=2.5×145.2=363 Rs.
4. Cost of remaining 2.5 kg =2.5×132=330 Rs.
5. Add Type C: extra cost=1×180=180 Rs; new total cost=330+180=510 Rs; new qty=3.5 kg.
6. Selling price per kg for second part is same as step 2 =145.2 Rs.
7. Revenue from second part=3.5×145.2=508.2 Rs.
8. Total revenue=363+508.2=871.2 Rs; total cost=660+180=840 Rs; profit=31.2 Rs.
9. Overall profit % = (31.2/840)×100≈3.71 %

questions.text: Machine A produces 120 units in 4 hrs, Machine B 150 units in 5 hrs and Machine C 180 units in 6 hrs. Each machine works continuously for 2 hrs and then undergoes a 30‑minute maintenance break, after which it resumes the same pattern. All three machines start together at 9:00 AM. When will the total cumulative production first reach or exceed 1000 units?
questions.solution:
1. Rate of each machine: A=120/4=30 u/h, B=150/5=30 u/h, C=180/6=30 u/h. Combined rate when all run =90 u/h.
2. In each 2 h working period all three work, then a 0.5 h joint break. Production per full cycle (2 h work + 0.5 h break) =90 u/h × 2 h =180 units.
3. Number of complete cycles needed: 1000 ÷ 180 =5 remainder 100. So 5 full cycles give 900 units.
4. Time for 5 cycles =5 × 2.5 h =12.5 h.
5. After the 5th break all machines are idle; they start working together again.
6. Remaining 100 units at 90 u/h need 100/90 h =1.111… h =1 h 6 min 40 s.
7. Total time =12.5 h +1.111… h =13.611… h =13 h 36 min 40 s.
8. Starting from 9:00 AM, add 13 h 36 min 40 s → 10:36 PM (approximately 10:36 PM).

questions.text: A trader purchases 1200 kg of mixed nuts. He buys almonds at Rs 200 per kg and cashews at Rs 350 per kg and mixes them in the ratio 3:2 by weight. He sells the whole mixture at a single price per kilogram. On the almonds portion he earns a 30 % profit, while on the cashews portion he incurs a 10 % loss. After calculating the total selling amount, he offers a flat 5 % discount on the entire bill. What is the overall profit percentage on the whole batch after the discount?
questions.solution:
Almond weight = 3/5 × 1200 = 720 kg; cost = 720 × 200 = Rs 144,000.
Cashew weight = 480 kg; cost = 480 × 350 = Rs 168,000.
Total cost = Rs 312,000.
Revenue from almonds = 144,000 × 1.30 = Rs 187,200.
Revenue from cashews = 168,000 × 0.90 = Rs 151,200.
Total revenue before discount = Rs 338,400.
After 5 % discount: 338,400 × 0.95 = Rs 321,480.
Profit = 321,480 – 312,000 = Rs 9,480.
Profit % = (9,480 / 312,000) × 100 ≈ 3 %.

questions.text: In the following sentence, one word is incorrectly used. Identify the word that should be replaced to convey the intended meaning: “The committee’s decision was *inevitable*, as the evidence clearly pointed to the defendant’s innocence.”
questions.solution: The sentence intends to say the decision was unavoidable because evidence showed innocence. ‘Inevitable’ means unavoidable, usually implying something certain to happen, often negative. Here the intended meaning is that the decision was *unavoidable* due to clear evidence of innocence, so the correct word should be ‘inevitable’. However, the context requires a word meaning ‘justified’ or ‘inevitable’? Actually the error is that ‘inevitable’ suggests the decision was bound to happen regardless of evidence, which is opposite. The correct replacement is ‘inevitable’ → ‘inevitable’ is wrong; the word to replace is ‘inevitable’. Hence option A.

questions.text:
Read the following passage and choose the word that best replaces the underlined word without altering the meaning of the sentence.

"The minister's speech was **replete** with platitudes, yet the audience remained indifferent."

Which of the following words can replace the underlined word?
questions.solution: The word 'replete' means 'filled' or 'abundant'. Option B conveys the same meaning. Options A, C and D are opposites, leading to a change in meaning.

questions.text:
Read the following passage and choose the option that best replaces the underlined phrase without changing the meaning of the passage.

"During the annual harvest festival, the village council decided to **let the cat out of the bag** about the new irrigation scheme, fearing that secrecy would only breed rumors. However, the elders argued that revealing the plan prematurely might **throw a wrench into** the farmers' preparations, as they were still arranging the logistics. After a heated debate, the council chose to **keep the lid on** the scheme until the sowing season began, ensuring that the information would be released at the most opportune moment."

Which of the following replacements for the underlined phrase "let the cat out of the bag" is most appropriate?
questions.solution: The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret. Among the options, only "spill the beans" is a synonymous idiom meaning to disclose information. "Break the ice" means to initiate conversation, "turn a blind eye" means to ignore, and "beat around the bush" means to avoid the main point. Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: A sum of money is invested at a simple interest rate of 5% per annum for the first 2 years. After these 2 years, the rate is increased to 7% per annum for the remaining 3 years. If the total interest earned at the end of 5 years is Rs 1550, what was the original principal amount?
questions.solution:
Let principal = P.
Interest for first 2 years = P×5%×2 = 0.10P.
Interest for next 3 years = P×7%×3 = 0.21P.
Total interest = 0.10P + 0.21P = 0.31P.
Given total interest = Rs 1550 → 0.31P = 1550.
P = 1550 ÷ 0.31 = 1550 × 100 ÷ 31 = 155000 ÷ 31 = 5000.
Thus the principal is Rs 5,000.

questions.text: A sum of Rs.1000 is invested at an annual compound interest rate of 8%. After completing 3 years, the bank gives a one‑time cash rebate equal to 5% of the amount that has accrued up to that point, and the rebate is immediately withdrawn. The remaining amount then continues to earn interest at the same 8% rate for another 2 years. What is the total amount (in rupees) after the full 5‑year period?

A tea vendor mixes 10 kg of Type A tea costing Rs 150 per kg with an unknown quantity of Type B tea costing Rs 90 per kg. The resulting blend sells for Rs 120 per kg. He then sells 8 kg of this blend and adds more Type B tea to the remaining mixture, after which the new blend sells for Rs 108 per kg. How many kilograms of Type B tea were used in the initial mixing?
questions.solution:
Let x kg be the initial amount of Type B.
Cost equation: (10×150 + x×90)/(10+x)=120
=>1500+90x = 1200+120x
=>300 = 30x ⇒ x = 10 kg.
Total weight =20 kg, total cost =1500+900=2400 Rs.
After selling 8 kg (cost 8×120=960 Rs), remaining weight =12 kg, cost =2400‑960=1440 Rs.
Add y kg of Type B (cost 90y) and new price becomes 108 Rs/kg:
(1440+90y)/(12+y)=108
=>1440+90y = 1296+108y
=>144 = 18y ⇒ y = 8 kg (consistent, confirming the data).
Thus the initial amount of Type B was 10 kg.
questions.topic: Mixture – sequential blending with price change

questions.text: Machine A can produce 120 widgets in 8 hours. Machine B produces 30 % more widgets per hour than Machine A. Both machines work together for 5 hours and then Machine B breaks down. The remaining Machine A continues working alone until a total of 1500 widgets are produced. What is the total time (in hours) taken to complete the production?
questions.solution:
1. Rate of Machine A = 120/8 = 15 widgets/hr.
2. Rate of Machine B = 15 × 1.30 = 19.5 widgets/hr.
3. Combined rate = 15 + 19.5 = 34.5 widgets/hr.
4. Production in first 5 hrs = 34.5 × 5 = 172.5 widgets.
5. Widgets left = 1500 – 172.5 = 1327.5 widgets.
6. Time for Machine A alone = 1327.5 ÷ 15 = 88.5 hrs.
7. Total time = 5 hrs + 88.5 hrs = 93.5 hrs.

questions.text: A retailer sells a gadget at Rs 60 per unit. A bulk buyer purchases 120 units. The retailer offers a 10% discount on the total bill if the buyer purchases at least 100 units. Moreover, if the amount payable after this discount exceeds Rs 5,000, the retailer gives an additional cash rebate of Rs 200. What is the final amount the buyer has to pay?
questions.solution:
1. Total price = 120 × 60 = Rs 7,200.
2. Since quantity ≥100, apply 10% discount: 10% of 7,200 = Rs 720.
3. Amount after discount = 7,200 - 720 = Rs 6,480.
4. Because Rs 6,480 > 5,000, give rebate of Rs 200.
5. Final payable = 6,480 - 200 = Rs 6,280.

questions.text: A shopkeeper purchases 200 kg of rice at Rs 40 per kg. He sells 120 kg at a 25 % profit on cost and the remaining 80 kg at a 10 % loss on cost. On the total sale amount a sales tax of 5 % is levied, which he pays out of the receipts. After paying the tax, he gives the buyer a discount of 2 % on the post‑tax amount. What is the overall profit percentage earned by the shopkeeper on the whole transaction?

A dealer purchases 500 units of a gadget at Rs 120 each. He sells 60 % of the units at a profit of 25 % on cost and the remaining units at a loss of 10 % on cost. He offers a cash discount of 5 % on the total selling price if the buyer pays within 15 days. The buyer pays after 45 days, i.e., 30 days late, and is charged simple interest at 12 % per annum on the discounted amount for the delayed period. What is the net amount the buyer has to pay (in rupees)?
questions.solution:
1. Total cost =500×120=Rs 60,000.
2. Profit sale: 60% of 500 =300 units; selling price per unit =120×1.25=Rs 150; revenue =300×150=Rs 45,000.
3. Loss sale: remaining 200 units; selling price per unit =120×0.90=Rs 108; revenue =200×108=Rs 21,600.
4. Total selling price =45,000+21,600=Rs 66,600.
5. Discount 5% =0.05×66,600=Rs 3,330; discounted price =66,600‑3,330=Rs 63,270.
6. Delay =30 days; simple interest =63,270×12%×(30/365)=63,270×0.12×0.0821918≈Rs 624.
7. Net amount =63,270+624=Rs 63,894.
questions.style: Tiered Discount with Conditional Simple Interest

questions.text: Despite his usual ______ nature, he acted generously on this occasion.
questions.solution:
1. The word “generously” signals a positive, giving attitude.
2. The phrase “Despite his usual … nature” requires a word opposite in meaning to “generously”.
3. The antonym of generous is miserly (stingy).
4. Among the options, only “miserly” fits this antonym requirement.

questions.text: Select the one word that best substitutes the following expression: "A person who has an excessive enthusiasm for collecting books."
questions.solution:
